questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the effective nuclear charge felt by one 4p electron of a neutral bromine atom (Z = 35), whose configuration is $[Ar]3d^{10}4s^2 4p^5$.
questions.explanation: The six other 4s/4p electrons screen $0.35$ each for $2.10$. The eighteen electrons in the 3s, 3p and 3d shells screen $0.85$ each for $15.30$, and the ten 1s, 2s and 2p electrons screen $1.00$ each for $10.00$. Total screening is $27.40$, so $Z_{eff} = 35 - 27.40 = 7.60$. Copying the selenium value gives 6.95, reporting total screening gives 27.40, and treating the 3d electrons at 1.00 gives 6.10.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: What percentage of the nuclear charge of a selenium atom (Z = 34, $[Ar]3d^{10}4s^2 4p^4$) is screened from one 4p electron by the other electrons, rounded to the nearest whole percent?
questions.explanation: The five other 4s/4p electrons screen $0.35$ each for $1.75$. The eighteen 3s/3p/3d electrons screen $0.85$ each for $15.30$, and the ten inner electrons screen $10.00$. Total screening is $27.05$, and $27.05/34 = 0.7956$, which rounds to 80 percent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Find the effective nuclear charge felt by one 4p electron of an arsenic atom (Z = 33, $[Ar]3d^{10}4s^2 4p^3$), multiply it by 10, and report the nearest integer.
questions.explanation: The four other 4s/4p electrons screen $0.35$ each for $1.40$. The eighteen 3s/3p/3d electrons screen $0.85$ each for $15.30$, and the ten inner electrons screen $10.00$. Total screening is $26.70$, so $Z_{eff} = 33 - 26.70 = 6.30$ and $10 \times 6.30 = 63$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: What percentage of the nuclear charge of a bromide ion ($Br^{-}$, Z = 35, 36 electrons) is screened from one 4p electron, rounded to the nearest whole percent?
questions.explanation: The seven other 4s/4p electrons screen $0.35$ each for $2.45$. The eighteen 3s/3p/3d electrons screen $0.85$ each for $15.30$, and the ten inner electrons screen $10.00$. Total screening is $27.75$, and $27.75/35 = 0.7929$, which rounds to 79 percent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Two bonded atoms have Pauling electronegativities of 2.20 for hydrogen and 2.96 for bromine. Estimate the percentage ionic character of the H-Br bond, rounded to the nearest whole percent.
questions.explanation: The difference is $\Delta\chi = 2.96 - 2.20 = 0.76$, so $\Delta\chi^2/4 = 0.5776/4 = 0.144$. The ionic character is $100(1 - e^{-0.144}) = 100(1 - 0.866) = 13.4$, which rounds to 13.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Hypothetical atoms P and Q have single-bond energies of 150 kJ/mol (P-P), 250 kJ/mol (Q-Q) and 390 kJ/mol (P-Q). Estimate the Pauling electronegativity difference between P and Q to two decimal places.
questions.explanation: The excess bond energy is $\Delta = 390 - \sqrt{150 \times 250} = 390 - 193.65 = 196.35$ kJ/mol. Pauling's relation $\Delta = 96.5(\chi_P - \chi_Q)^2$ gives $(\chi_P - \chi_Q)^2 = 2.03$, so the difference is $\sqrt{2.03} = 1.43$. Reporting the squared value gives 2.03, inverting the answer gives 0.70, and a rounded wrong bond energy gives 1.20.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In a Moseley-type relation the square root of the X-ray frequency equals 7 times (Z minus 1), in chosen units. A line has a square-root frequency of 245 units. What is the atomic number of the emitting element?
questions.explanation: Dividing the square-root frequency by 7 gives $Z - 1 = 245/7 = 35$. Adding 1 gives $Z = 36$, which corresponds to krypton.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Find the mean first ionisation enthalpy, in kJ/mol to the nearest whole number, of oxygen (1314), sulphur (1000) and selenium (941) taken together.
questions.explanation: The sum is $1314 + 1000 + 941 = 3255$ kJ/mol. Dividing by 3 gives $3255/3 = 1085$ kJ/mol. Reporting only the sulphur value gives 1000, averaging just O and S gives 1157, and reporting Se alone gives 941.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the percentage ionic character of the H-Cl bond using Pauling electronegativities of 2.20 for H and 3.16 for Cl, rounded to the nearest whole percent.
questions.explanation: The difference is $\Delta\chi = 3.16 - 2.20 = 0.96$, so $\Delta\chi^2/4 = 0.9216/4 = 0.230$. The ionic character is $100(1 - e^{-0.230}) = 100(1 - 0.795) = 20.5$, which rounds to 21.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Compare the effective nuclear charges felt by the 4p electrons of bromine (Z = 35) and selenium (Z = 34). What is the ratio of the bromine value to the selenium value, to two decimal places?
questions.explanation: Bromine 4p gives $Z_{eff} = 7.60$, and selenium 4p gives $Z_{eff} = 34 - 27.05 = 6.95$. The ratio is $7.60/6.95 = 1.094$, which rounds to 1.09. Inverting the ratio gives 0.91, taking the difference gives 0.65, and quoting the bromine value alone gives 7.60.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Find the difference between the effective nuclear charges felt by one 4p electron of bromine (Z = 35) and of arsenic (Z = 33). Multiply the difference by 10 and report the nearest integer.
questions.explanation: Bromine 4p gives $Z_{eff} = 7.60$ and arsenic 4p gives $Z_{eff} = 6.30$. The difference is $1.30$, and $10 \times 1.30 = 13$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the effective nuclear charge felt by one 3s electron of a phosphorus atom (Z = 15, $[Ne]3s^2 3p^3$). Multiply the value by 10 and report the nearest integer.
questions.explanation: The four other 3s/3p electrons screen $0.35$ each for $1.40$. The eight 2s/2p electrons screen $0.85$ each for $6.80$, and the 1s pair screens $2.00$. Total screening is $10.20$, so $Z_{eff} = 15 - 10.20 = 4.80$ and $10 \times 4.80 = 48$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: What percentage of the nuclear charge of a chloride ion ($Cl^{-}$, Z = 17, 18 electrons) is screened from one 3p electron, rounded to the nearest whole percent?
questions.explanation: The seven other 3s/3p electrons screen $0.35$ each for $2.45$. The eight 2s/2p electrons screen $0.85$ each for $6.80$, and the 1s pair screens $2.00$. Total screening is $11.25$, and $11.25/17 = 0.6618$, which rounds to 66 percent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Compute the mean Pauling electronegativity of the four halogens F (3.98), Cl (3.16), Br (2.96) and I (2.66), to two decimal places.
questions.explanation: The sum is $3.98 + 3.16 + 2.96 + 2.66 = 12.76$. Dividing by 4 gives $12.76/4 = 3.19$. Reporting the Cl value gives 3.16, averaging only F and I gives 3.32, and reporting the Br value gives 2.96.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Find the 3p effective nuclear charges of phosphorus (Z = 15) and silicon (Z = 14), subtract the silicon value from the phosphorus value, multiply the difference by 100, and report the integer.
questions.explanation: Phosphorus 3p gives $Z_{eff} = 15 - 10.20 = 4.80$ and silicon 3p gives $Z_{eff} = 14 - 9.85 = 4.15$. The difference is $0.65$, and $100 \times 0.65 = 65$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the first ionisation enthalpies of Group 16 elements. I. O has a higher IE1 than S. II. S has a higher IE1 than Se. III. Te has a higher IE1 than Se. Which option is correct?
questions.explanation: O (1314) is higher than S (1000), so I is true. S (1000) is higher than Se (941), so II is true. Te (869) is lower than Se (941), so III is false, since IE1 falls down the group.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider these comparisons among halogen species. (i) $Br^{-}$ has a larger ionic radius than $Cl^{-}$. (ii) Br has a less negative electron gain enthalpy than Cl. (iii) HF is a weaker acid than HCl in water. (iv) I is more electronegative than Br. How many of these four statements are correct?
questions.explanation: $Br^{-}$ (196 pm) is larger than $Cl^{-}$ (181 pm), so (i) is correct. Br (-325) is less negative than Cl (-349), so (ii) is correct. HF is a weak acid in water while HCl is strong, so (iii) is correct. I (2.66) is less electronegative than Br (2.96), so (iv) is false. Three statements are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the acidity of the hydrogen halides in aqueous solution. I. HF is the weakest acid among the hydrogen halides. II. HI is the strongest acid among the hydrogen halides. III. HCl is stronger than HBr. Which option is correct?
questions.explanation: HF is a weak acid in water while the others are strong, so I is true. HI has the weakest H-X bond and is the strongest acid, so II is true. HBr is stronger than HCl because its H-Br bond is weaker, so III is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the chemistry of beryllium oxide and its neighbours in the periodic table. I. BeO is amphoteric. II. Be(OH)$_2$ dissolves in excess NaOH. III. BeO is more basic than MgO. Which option is correct?
questions.explanation: BeO reacts with both acids and strong bases, so I is true. Be(OH)$_2$ dissolves in excess NaOH to form a beryllate ion, so II is true. MgO is the more basic oxide because Be$^{2+}$ is small and highly polarising, so III is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the percentage ionic characters estimated for NaCl (71), HF (55), HCl (21), HBr (13) and MgO (68). How many of these bonds are more than 50 percent ionic?
questions.explanation: NaCl (71), HF (55) and MgO (68) exceed 50 percent, while HCl (21) and HBr (13) do not. The count is 3.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Compare the 4p effective nuclear charges of these atoms. I. The 4p electrons of Br feel a higher value than those of Se. II. The 4p electrons of As feel a lower value than those of Se. III. The 4p electrons of Se feel a higher value than those of Br. Which option is correct?
questions.explanation: Br 4p gives $Z_{eff} = 7.60$, above Se at 6.95, so I is true. As 4p gives 6.30, below Se at 6.95, so II is true. Se 4p at 6.95 is lower than Br 4p at 7.60, so III is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The effective nuclear charges felt by 4p electrons are 6.95 for Se and 7.60 for Br. What is the percentage increase going from the Se value to the Br value, rounded to the nearest whole percent?
questions.explanation: The increase is $7.60 - 6.95 = 0.65$. Relative to the Se value, $0.65/6.95 = 0.0935$, or 9.35 percent, which rounds to 9.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the Pauling electronegativities of Br (2.96), I (2.66) and Te (2.10). I. Br is more electronegative than I. II. I is more electronegative than Te. III. Te is more electronegative than Se. Which option is correct?
questions.explanation: Br (2.96) exceeds I (2.66), so I is true. I (2.66) exceeds Te (2.10), so II is true. Se (2.55) exceeds Te (2.10), so III is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The first ionisation enthalpies are 1000 kJ/mol for S and 941 kJ/mol for Se. What is the percentage by which the IE1 of Se is lower than that of S, rounded to the nearest whole percent?
questions.explanation: The difference is $1000 - 941 = 59$ kJ/mol. Relative to S, the drop is $59/1000 = 0.059$, or 5.9 percent, which rounds to 6.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider metallic character in the p-block. I. Bi is more metallic than Sb. II. As is more metallic than P. III. N is a metalloid. Which option is correct?
questions.explanation: Bi is the more metallic member of Group 15 compared with Sb, so I is true. As is more metallic than P, so II is true. N is a non-metal and not a metalloid, so III is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider these comparisons for Group 16. (i) IE1 of S is higher than IE1 of Se. (ii) IE1 of Se is higher than IE1 of Te. (iii) Electron gain enthalpy of Se is more negative than that of S. (iv) The atomic radius of Te is larger than that of Se. How many of these statements are correct?
questions.explanation: S (1000) exceeds Se (941), so (i) is correct. Se (941) exceeds Te (869), so (ii) is correct. Se (-195) is less negative than S (-200), so (iii) is false. Te has a larger radius than Se, so (iv) is correct. Three statements are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Compare the 4p effective nuclear charges of these atoms. I. Ga has a lower 4p value than Ge. II. Ge has a lower 4p value than As. III. As has a higher 4p value than Br. Which option is correct?
questions.explanation: Ga 4p gives 5.00 and Ge 4p gives 5.65, so I is true. Ge 4p is 5.65 and As 4p is 6.30, so II is true. As 4p (6.30) is lower than Br 4p (7.60), so III is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Compute the ratio of the 4p effective nuclear charge of selenium to that of arsenic, multiply it by 10, and report the nearest integer.
questions.explanation: Selenium 4p gives $Z_{eff} = 6.95$ and arsenic 4p gives $Z_{eff} = 6.30$. The ratio is $6.95/6.30 = 1.103$, and $10 \times 1.103 = 11.03$, which rounds to 11.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the electron gain enthalpies of halogens. I. Cl has a more negative electron gain enthalpy than F. II. I has a less negative electron gain enthalpy than Br. III. Br has a more negative electron gain enthalpy than F. Which option is correct?
questions.explanation: Cl (-349) is more negative than F (-328), so I is true. I (-295) is less negative than Br (-325), so II is true. Br (-325) is less negative than F (-328), so III is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the ions $Br^{-}$, $Rb^{+}$, $Sr^{2+}$, $Se^{2-}$ and $Cl^{-}$. How many of these ions are isoelectronic with krypton (36 electrons)?
questions.explanation: $Br^{-}$ (35 + 1 = 36), $Rb^{+}$ (37 - 1 = 36), $Sr^{2+}$ (38 - 2 = 36) and $Se^{2-}$ (34 + 2 = 36) all have 36 electrons. $Cl^{-}$ has 18 electrons and does not qualify, so the count is 4.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Compare the first ionisation enthalpies of Group 2 elements. I. Ba has a lower IE1 than Ca. II. Sr has a higher IE1 than Ba. III. Ca has a lower IE1 than Sr. Which option is correct?
questions.explanation: Ba (503) is lower than Ca (590), so I is true. Sr (549) is higher than Ba (503), so II is true. Ca (590) is higher than Sr (549), so III is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The first ionisation enthalpies are 941 kJ/mol for Se and 869 kJ/mol for Te. What is the percentage by which the IE1 of Te is lower than that of Se, rounded to the nearest whole percent?
questions.explanation: The difference is $941 - 869 = 72$ kJ/mol. Relative to Se, the drop is $72/941 = 0.0765$, or 7.65 percent, which rounds to 8.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Compute the ratio of the first ionisation enthalpy of Ne (2081 kJ/mol) to that of Ar (1521 kJ/mol), to two decimal places.
questions.explanation: The ratio is $2081/1521 = 1.368$, which rounds to 1.37. Inverting the ratio gives 0.73, dividing the difference in thousands gives 0.56, and reporting the Ne value alone gives 2081.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the first ionisation enthalpies of O (1314), S (1000), Se (941) and Te (869) kJ/mol. How many of these four elements have IE1 below 1000 kJ/mol?
questions.explanation: Only Se (941) and Te (869) are below 1000 kJ/mol. S sits exactly at 1000 and O is higher, so the count is 2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the effective nuclear charge felt by one 3d electron of a gallium atom (Z = 31, $[Ar]3d^{10}4s^2 4p^1$), where the 4s and 4p electrons do not screen 3d electrons.
questions.explanation: The nine other 3d electrons screen $0.35$ each for $3.15$. The eighteen electrons in the 1s to 3p shells screen $1.00$ each for $18.00$. Total screening is $21.15$, so $Z_{eff} = 31 - 21.15 = 9.85$. Copying the Ga 4p value gives 5.00, ignoring the 3s and 3p shielding gives 17.85, and reporting total screening gives 21.15.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the effective nuclear charges of selected p-block valence electrons and ions, estimated with standard screening constants. Which of the following statements are correct? Select all that apply.
options: A) The 4p electrons of Br feel a higher effective nuclear charge than those of Se, about $7.60$ against $6.95$.
B) The 4p electrons of As feel a higher effective nuclear charge than those of Br, about $6.30$ against $7.60$.
C) The 4p electrons of $Br^{-}$ feel a lower effective nuclear charge than those of neutral Br, about $7.25$ against $7.60$.
D) The 4p electrons of $Se^{2-}$ feel a higher effective nuclear charge than the 5p electrons of Te, about $6.25$ against $6.95$.
questions.explanation: Br 4p gives $35 - 27.40 = 7.60$ and Se 4p gives $34 - 27.05 = 6.95$, so A is correct. As 4p gives $33 - 26.70 = 6.30$, below Br's 7.60, so B is false. $Br^{-}$ 4p gives $35 - 27.75 = 7.25$, below neutral Br at 7.60, so C is correct. $Se^{2-}$ 4p gives $34 - 27.75 = 6.25$, which is lower than Te 5p at 6.95, so D is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Using Pauling electronegativities (H 2.20, Se 2.55, Br 2.96, As 2.18, I 2.66, Te 2.10) and the usual percentage ionic character estimate, which statements are correct? Select all that apply.
options: A) The Se-Br bond is less than 5 percent ionic.
B) The Te-I bond is more than 10 percent ionic.
C) The As-Br bond is less than 15 percent ionic.
D) The H-I bond is more than 5 percent ionic.
questions.explanation: For Se-Br, $\Delta\chi = 0.41$ gives $100(1 - e^{-0.042}) = 4.1$ percent, so A is correct. For Te-I, $\Delta\chi = 0.56$ gives $100(1 - e^{-0.078}) \approx 7.5$ percent, so B is false. For As-Br, $\Delta\chi = 0.78$ gives $100(1 - e^{-0.152}) \approx 14.1$ percent, so C is correct. For H-I, $\Delta\chi = 0.46$ gives $100(1 - e^{-0.053}) \approx 5.2$ percent, so D is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the first ionisation enthalpies and electron gain enthalpies of selected p-block elements. Which of the following statements are correct? Select all that apply, using standard textbook values.
options: A) The first ionisation enthalpy of Te (869 kJ/mol) is lower than that of Se (941 kJ/mol).
B) The first ionisation enthalpy of As (947 kJ/mol) exceeds that of Se (941 kJ/mol).
C) The first ionisation enthalpy of Br (1140 kJ/mol) exceeds that of Se (941 kJ/mol).
D) The first ionisation enthalpy of Ga (579 kJ/mol) exceeds that of Ge (762 kJ/mol).
questions.explanation: Te $(869)$ is below Se $(941)$, so A is correct. As $(947)$ is just above Se $(941)$ because of the half-filled $4p^3$ subshell, so B is correct. Br $(1140)$ lies well above Se $(941)$ across the period, so C is correct. Ga $(579)$ is far below Ge $(762)$, so D is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Using usual screening conventions, estimate the 4p effective nuclear charge of bromine and of the bromide ion $Br^{-}$. Divide the neutral bromine value by the ion value and round the ratio to the nearest integer.
questions.explanation: Neutral Br 4p gives $35 - 27.40 = 7.60$ and $Br^{-}$ 4p gives $35 - 27.75 = 7.25$. The ratio $7.60/7.25 = 1.05$ rounds to 1.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the effective nuclear charge felt by one 4p electron of a krypton atom (Z = 36, $[Ar]3d^{10}4s^2 4p^6$), using the usual screening conventions. Which value is correct?
questions.explanation: The seven other 4s/4p electrons screen $0.35$ each for $2.45$. The eighteen 3s, 3p and 3d electrons screen $0.85$ each for $15.30$, and the ten inner electrons screen $1.00$ each for $10.00$. Total screening is $27.75$, so $Z_{eff} = 36 - 27.75 = 8.25$. Copying the bromide value gives 7.25, ignoring the 3d shielding gives 16.75, and reporting total screening gives 27.75.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the sizes and electron gain enthalpies of selected p-block ions and atoms. Which of the following statements are correct? Select all that apply.
options: A) The ionic radius of $Br^{-}$ (196 pm) is larger than that of $Cl^{-}$ (181 pm).
B) The ionic radius of $Sr^{2+}$ (118 pm) is smaller than that of $Rb^{+}$ (152 pm).
C) The ionic radius of $Se^{2-}$ (198 pm) is smaller than that of $Te^{2-}$ (221 pm).
D) The ionic radius of $Br^{-}$ (196 pm) is larger than that of $Se^{2-}$ (198 pm).
questions.explanation: Going down a group increases ionic size, and $Br^{-}$ (196) exceeds $Cl^{-}$ (181), so A is correct. $Sr^{2+}$ (118) is smaller than $Rb^{+}$ (152), so B is correct. $Se^{2-}$ (198) is smaller than $Te^{2-}$ (221), so C is correct. $Br^{-}$ (196) is smaller than $Se^{2-}$ (198) because the two extra electrons on $Se^{2-}$ enlarge its cloud, so D is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Count how many of the following statements about krypton and xenon are correct. (i) The first ionisation enthalpy of Ar is higher than that of Kr. (ii) The first ionisation enthalpy of Kr is higher than that of Xe. (iii) The first ionisation enthalpy of Ne is lower than that of He. (iv) The 4p effective nuclear charge of Br is higher than that of Kr.
questions.explanation: Ar $(1521)$ is above Kr $(1351)$ kJ/mol, so (i) is correct. Kr $(1351)$ is above Xe $(1170)$, so (ii) is correct. He $(2372)$ is higher than Ne $(2081)$, so (iii) is false. The Kr 4p value of $Z_{eff} = 8.25$ exceeds the Br 4p value of $7.60$, so (iv) is false. Two statements are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the effective nuclear charge experienced by one 5p electron of a neutral tin atom (Z = 50, $[Kr]4d^{10}5s^2 5p^2$), using the usual screening conventions. Which value is correct?
questions.explanation: The three other 5s/5p electrons screen $0.35$ each for $1.05$. The eighteen 4s, 4p and 4d electrons screen $0.85$ each for $15.30$. The twenty-eight electrons in the 1s to 3d shells screen $1.00$ each for $28.00$. Total screening is $44.35$, so $Z_{eff} = 50 - 44.35 = 5.65$. Copying a 6.35 value from a lighter element is a common slip, treating the 4d electrons as fully shielding gives 4.15, and reporting total screening gives 44.35.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the effective nuclear charge experienced by one 5p electron of a neutral tellurium atom (Z = 52, $[Kr]4d^{10}5s^2 5p^4$), using the usual screening conventions. Which value is correct?
questions.explanation: The five other 5s/5p electrons screen $0.35$ each for $1.75$. The eighteen 4s, 4p and 4d electrons screen $0.85$ each for $15.30$. The twenty-eight electrons in the 1s to 3d shells screen $1.00$ each for $28.00$. Total screening is $45.05$, so $Z_{eff} = 52 - 45.05 = 6.95$. Copying the bromine 4p value gives 7.60, ignoring the 4d shielding gives 15.45, and reporting total screening gives 45.05.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Divide the 5p effective nuclear charge of neutral tellurium by that of neutral tin, both estimated with usual screening conventions, and round the ratio to the nearest integer.
questions.explanation: Tellurium 5p gives $52 - 45.05 = 6.95$ and tin 5p gives $50 - 44.35 = 5.65$. The ratio $6.95/5.65 = 1.23$ rounds to 1.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the effective nuclear charge felt by one 4p electron of the selenide ion $Se^{2-}$ (Z = 34, 36 electrons, $[Kr]$), using the usual screening conventions. Which value is correct?
questions.explanation: The seven other 4s/4p electrons screen $0.35$ each for $2.45$. The eighteen 3s, 3p and 3d electrons screen $0.85$ each for $15.30$, and the ten inner electrons screen $10.00$. Total screening is $27.75$, so $Z_{eff} = 34 - 27.75 = 6.25$. The neutral selenium value is 6.95, the bromide value is 7.25, and 27.75 is the total screening.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Count how many of these effective nuclear charges exceed 6.00: the 4p value of $Se^{2-}$, the 4p value of $Br^{-}$, the 5p value of neutral Te, the 5p value of neutral Sn, and the 3d value of neutral Ga (Z = 31).
questions.explanation: The values are $Se^{2-}$ 6.25, $Br^{-}$ 7.25, Te 5p 6.95, Sn 5p 5.65 and Ga 3d 9.85. Four of them (all except Sn 5p) exceed 6.00, so the count is 4.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the percentage ionic character of the Te-I bond using Pauling electronegativities of 2.10 for Te and 2.66 for I, rounded to the nearest whole percent.
questions.explanation: The difference is $\Delta\chi = 0.56$, so $\Delta\chi^2/4 = 0.3136/4 = 0.0784$. The ionic character is $100(1 - e^{-0.0784}) = 100(1 - 0.9246) = 7.54$, which rounds to 8. Quoting the covalent fraction gives 92, reporting the raw difference gives 56, and rounding the value down gives 7.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Arrange the 4p effective nuclear charges of As (Z = 33), Se (Z = 34), Br (Z = 35) and Kr (Z = 36) from lowest to highest, using usual screening conventions. Which ordering is correct?
questions.explanation: The computed 4p values are $6.30$ (As), $6.95$ (Se), $7.60$ (Br) and $8.25$ (Kr), which increase steadily across the period. Option B places Se below As, option C places Br below Se, and option D places Kr below Br.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the effective nuclear charges of selected valence and inner electrons of germanium (Z = 32, $[Ar]3d^{10}4s^2 4p^2$) and nearby atoms, using usual screening conventions. Which of the following statements are correct? Select all that apply.
options: A) The 4s electrons of Ge feel about the same effective nuclear charge as its 4p electrons.
B) The 4s electrons of Ge feel a higher effective nuclear charge than the 4s electrons of Ga.
C) The 4s electrons of Zn feel a higher effective nuclear charge than those of Ge.
D) The 4s electrons of Ge feel a higher effective nuclear charge than its 3d electrons.
questions.explanation: Ge 4s gives $Z_{eff} = 32 - 26.35 = 5.65$, the same as Ge 4p, so A is correct. Ga 4s gives $31 - 26.00 = 5.00$, below Ge's 5.65, so B is correct. Zn 4s gives $30 - 25.65 = 4.35$, which is lower than Ge's value, so C is false. Ge 3d gives $32 - 21.15 = 10.85$, far above the 4s value, so D is false.
